events.text: North dome shutter service will free the sticking lower shutter without altering the telescope mount. The job begins with a visual check of the latch and rail. A separate optical alignment crew is using the annex tonight.

Guide-camera bracket realignment concerns the small camera under the north telescope saddle. The work stops at the bracket interface and excludes shutter repair. Record the mounting washers in order before undoing the retaining nut.

events.locator: Extracted intake image annotation, lower-left label
events.text: The North dome shutter service intake photograph shows a violet chalk cross beside the old lower latch. The time stamp is partly cropped, but the chalk mark is clear. This image predates cleaning and is retained only as intake evidence.

North dome shutter service and Guide-camera bracket realignment use isolation permit D17 for the shared dome power cutoff. Each crew must sign its own completion box before power returns. The permit does not combine the repair and alignment records.

The small fastener packet belongs on the upper shelf, away from loose washers. No equipment name appears on the envelope. Its pencilled initials are smeared, and the photograph does not show the surrounding bench or any docket number.

events.reason: Assign the upper-shelf fastener packet photo to Guide-camera bracket realignment; that packet holds its bracket screws.

events.text: North dome shutter service completed its dry travel check with the shutter stopped at the yellow rail tab. The technician heard no scrape at that position. This note reports the stop cue only; it gives neither motor current nor rail clearance.

An observatory maintenance primer is background reading for North dome shutter service. The example shutter uses a different drive and latch, so its dimensions cannot be transferred to ours. The relevant paragraph describes keeping loose cloth away from rails.

The annex notice lists a public stargazing talk and asks visitors to use the side stairs. Its little moon diagram is a decoration. There are no service dockets, camera bracket details, or crew assignments in the notice.
